claim: The verifier template tells the agent to put a rejection reason in `claim`, but check accepts it only when the claim starts with a rejection word or a reject_reason field is present — neither is mentioned
scenario: A verifier rejects a finding and writes the row as verify.md:123 instructs: status and confidence 'rejected', claim 'No defect: the route is wrapped in RequirePermission, so the scenario is unreachable'. `import` takes it; `check` then exits 1 with 'rejected, but the reject reason is not recorded', because re.match at review.py:3084 anchors on отвергнут|отклонен|отклонён|не подтверд|rejected|not confirmed. A claim with the word in the middle fails too. The register goes red on a report written exactly by the instructions, and the way out is a lead command the verifier does not have. Same in verify.ru.md:123.
invariant: invariant 9 — a gate that demands what the role template does not announce turns an honest report red
root: check demands what no role template announces

claim: The draft-findings JSON schema in every role template omits `root` and `dup_of`, so the three-instance guard gate and the duplicate gate can never be satisfied by an agent following the template
scenario: A hunter finds five instances of one class, names it under **Root:** in the report as hunter.md:138-141 asks, and writes the JSON lines in the prescribed format, which has no root field. The register stores them without one: roots_of groups nothing, the guard gate at review.py:3305 stays silent, `review roots` prints 'no roots recorded', and the class is closed by five separate fixes — the outcome lesson 25 exists to prevent. dup_of is missing the same way: verify.md:70-76 and lesson 16 prescribe marking a duplicate and name no field, so check answers 'marked duplicate, but not of what exactly'. set-finding has no --root, so the draft file is the only road in.
invariant: invariant 1 — a gate that cannot go red on the state it exists to catch; invariant 9
root: the defect-class mechanism is announced in no document an agent or a lead reads

claim: SKILL.md documents `--round` only for the fix reviewer, so a second fix round overwrites round 1's fix report and the round-2 fixreview prompt points at a file nobody was told to write
scenario: Round 1 completes and the fix reviewer files medium findings. The lead starts round 2 as SKILL.md:92 says — `prompt <ID> --role fix`, no round. report_path names the report <ID>-<slug>.fix.md, so the round-2 fixer overwrites round 1's report. The lead then runs `prompt <ID> --role fixreview --diff … --round 2`, whose opening line resolves {{FIX_REPORT}} to <ID>-<slug>.fix-2.md — a path nothing wrote. Neither fix.md nor fix.ru.md carries a round marker, so nothing else signals the round to the fixer.
invariant: a review artefact is overwritten because the flag that prevents it is real and undocumented
root: the fix and fix-review round mechanism is not carried into the kit's documents

claim: The shipped toy example names a register finding id in a code comment — the practice fix.md rule 5 and the entry point forbid — and the id it cites is the wrong finding
scenario: Copy examples/toy into a fresh repository as its README instructs and run `review refs`: it prints 'src/billing/quota.ts:1: H1-001' and exits 1; `check` reports the same as a warning. Removing the id from the comment makes refs answer that no finding is named outside docs/review/. The one shipped example of a correct review state demonstrates the practice the kit forbids, and H1-001 is 'Empty role parses into a user session' in src/auth/session.ts — nothing to do with quotas.
invariant: no references to the review in code (fix.md rule 5, entry-point.md fixing rules, SKILL.md)
root: the kit's own gates are never run over examples/toy

claim: examples/toy does not pass `check`: its own README.md is owned by no block and covered by no exclusion, contradicting the example's instruction that check passes on it
scenario: Follow examples/toy/README.md:21-24 — copy the directory into a fresh git repository, commit, run check. The exclusions cover only docs/review/** and .gitignore, and neither block's paths reach README.md, so coverage_map puts it in unassigned and check exits 1 with '1 files belong to no block'; coverage exits 1 naming the same file, and coverage.tsv on disk lists four files without it. Adding README.md to the exclusions removes that line and nothing else. A first-time user sees the gate refuse the state the example exists to demonstrate.
invariant: the reference example of a green review must be green
root: the kit's own gates are never run over examples/toy

claim: The sample block definition violates the phase-order gate: the array runs phase 1, phase 2, phase 1, phase 3, and check refuses a phase that decreases along the array
scenario: A user sets up a review, opens assets/blocks.example.json — the file setup step 2 and three check_definition refusals point at — keeps its arrangement, fills in their own paths and runs check. Installed as a real blocks.json the sample answers 'H13: phase 1 comes after phase 2 — the blocks array is ordered by phase, because that is the execution order', and sorting its four blocks by phase removes exactly that line. The sample teaches the arrangement the gate rejects.
invariant: a sample the tool's own refusals point at must satisfy the tool's own gates

claim: The Russian banner asset carries the English banner verbatim: only the surrounding explanation is Russian, the text meant to be pasted is not translated
scenario: A project runs `review setup --project X --lang ru`, works through the setup checklist to step 5 ('The banner in the root instructions file'), opens the .ru.md asset and pastes lines 11-21 into its Russian CLAUDE.md. Everything after the separator is byte-for-byte the English banner of agent-banner.md. The banner that is supposed to stop a new session from starting a parallel review arrives in English, inside a document whose language the team chose deliberately, and the .ru.md suffix exists for exactly this purpose.
invariant: the bilingual contract — a string that exists in one language and not the other is a defect
root: the Russian half of the bilingual assets is unwired

claim: `setup --lang ru` names the English samples in its checklist, and the Russian copies of invariants.example, manifest.example, journal.example and agent-banner are referenced by nothing in the kit
scenario: cmd_setup selects the entry point by language at review.py:3486 and then hardcodes English names at lines 3509, 3511, 3513 and 3516. Run against an empty repository, `setup --project Проект --lang ru` writes a Russian blocks.json, a Russian invariants skeleton and a Russian docs/review/README.md, then prints a checklist pointing at invariants.example.md, blocks.example.json, manifest.example.md and agent-banner.md. A scan of every tracked file finds the four Russian samples named nowhere in the kit: they ship and the user has no way to discover them.
invariant: the bilingual contract; the entry point in the same function proves the selection was intended
root: the Russian half of the bilingual assets is unwired

claim: The entry point that setup copies into every project as docs/review/README.md is behind the tool: no fixreview role or report name, no fix gate, no import --append, and its prompts/ list omits fixreview.md
scenario: A lead session that knows nothing does what the file promises — one command and the full picture. It runs the diff review as step 8 describes, writes the report under a name of its own, then `set-status <ID> closed`; check answers 'closed with fixed findings, but there is no fix reviewer report', because the gate globs <ID>-<slug>.fixreview-*.md. Earlier, moving the next block to running, it meets a fix-gate refusal the entry point never warned it about. Neither file contains the strings fixreview, fix_gate, --append, restamp or backfill. Same in entry-point.ru.md.
invariant: invariant 9 applied to the scaffold the project actually reads
root: the fix and fix-review round mechanism is not carried into the kit's documents

claim: The fix reviewer is handed a diff of any size with no statement of that size and no mention of --scope, while the hunter's prompt carries a measured reading budget
scenario: The kit's own T1 round-1 diff was 193 KB. A lead runs `prompt <ID> --role fixreview --diff main...HEAD` on a range of that size. diff_text prepends --stat and pastes the whole range; rule 1 says 'the diff is pasted below in full — read it' with no condition, and nothing states the volume, the token order of magnitude or where the budget line runs — all of which volume_note states for the hunter's file list. {{VOLUME}} occurs only in the two hunter templates, and neither fix-review template names --scope. The agent reads what fits and reports on the whole diff.
invariant: the budget must stand in the assignment, not in the lead session's head (the reasoning volume_note was written on)

claim: Lesson 13 requires every deferred finding to be fixed or rejected before the review ends, while the tool and SKILL.md treat a deferred finding with a reason as an accepted risk that ships in the summary
scenario: A lead reads the lessons before the first block, as SKILL.md:161-162 instructs, and holds the review open at the end to resolve a dozen deferred findings that render_summary writes under 'Accepted risks (deferred with a reason)' and that the completion conditions of SKILL.md:143 and entry-point.md:69-70 do not mention at all; check demands only the reason, never the resolution. Read in the other order, the same lead treats the summary's accepted-risks section as a defect. Two documents of the kit give opposite answers to 'is the review finished'. Same in lessons.ru.md:53-55.
invariant: lesson 36 of the same file — a lesson that does not reach the rules is worse than no lesson

claim: The Makefile snippet defines no generic `review` target, while SKILL.md offers `make review` as an example value for the cli field that every hint is built from
scenario: A project pastes makefile-snippet.mk into its Makefile and, following SKILL.md:28-30, sets "cli": "make review" in blocks.json. project_cli then builds every hint and refusal from that string: `make review init`, `make review coverage`, `make review restamp H1`. Run against the shipped snippet, `make review init` answers 'No rule to make target review' and exits 2, because the snippet defines only review-init, review-status and the rest. The package.json snippet does define the generic target, which is why `npm run review --` works.
invariant: hints are assembled from CLI, and the shipped snippets must agree with what SKILL.md says cli may hold
root: shipped assets hardcode `make` as the project's CLI

claim: The toy's findings.md header holds the literal `<skill>` path while its blocks.json sets no `cli`, so the file can never equal the regenerated one and check is red in every copy of the example
scenario: render_findings_md writes the 'GENERATED by' header from CLI, which without a `cli` field in blocks.json is python3 plus the tool's real absolute path. The shipped file carries the placeholder `python3 <skill>/scripts/review.py`, which the tool never produces, so the by-content comparison at review.py:3106 can never succeed. Copy examples/toy into a fresh repository and run check, as its README instructs: it exits 1 with 'findings.md diverged from findings.jsonl' on top of the unowned README.md. Adding a matching `cli` field, together with that exclusion, makes check exit 0.
invariant: the reference example of a green review must be green
root: the kit's own gates are never run over examples/toy

claim: `roots`, the class view the three-instance guard gate rests on, is named by no message of the tool, by no line of SKILL.md and by no line of the entry point, so a lead cannot learn it exists
scenario: Of the 23 subcommands, four are absent from SKILL.md: hypotheses, refs, roots and version. The entry point installed by setup names hypotheses and version, and a check warning names refs; roots is in none of the three. A lead meets 'root X: 3 instances (…) and no guard' and wants the class before choosing a guard, but the refusal names only set-finding --rule and the first four ids, and the two documents it has say nothing. It reads the register by hand or records a guard on a partial list.
invariant: hypothesis 7 — every user-facing command is in SKILL.md or reachable from it
root: the defect-class mechanism is announced in no document an agent or a lead reads

claim: Both banner assets hardcode `make review-status` with no {{CLI}} placeholder, and setup substitutes nothing in them, so a project without a Makefile pastes a dead command into every session
scenario: A Go or Rust project with no Makefile runs setup and follows step 5 of its checklist, which only prints the path to agent-banner.md. The banner says to run `make review-status`. Pasted into the root instructions file, it tells every future session of that project to run a command that does not exist — in the one document whose purpose is to stop a session from starting a parallel review. The sibling asset entry-point.md carries {{CLI}} and is substituted at review.py:3488, so the mechanism exists and this file does not use it; the kit's own AGENTS.md banner names the real path instead.
invariant: rule 5 of AGENTS.md — hints are assembled from CLI, no `make review-check` in strings
root: shipped assets hardcode `make` as the project's CLI

claim: TemplateContractTest only checks that each agent field name occurs anywhere in a template, so prose satisfies it and the draft schemas it was written for are unguarded (fix review round 1, R1-001)
scenario: All four English role templates reverted to f1a44a0: the guard fails on dup_of, reject_reason and defer_reason but stays green on root, the half of T2-002 its claim leads with. Every fenced draft schema deleted from all eight templates: green on all 13 fields in both languages, while an agent following the templates writes findings the register cannot group.
invariant: invariant 2 — a guard that can be holed with the suite green is not a guard
root: class guard keyed on incidental syntax

claim: {{DIFF}} is replaced over the assembled body, so the manifest's own mentions of it get the diff too: the prompt carries it three times while {{DIFF_VOLUME}} states one (fix review round 1, R1-002)
scenario: prompt T2 --role fixreview --diff f1a44a0..HEAD states 464 KB, 4091 lines, ~104k tokens and delivers 1410 KB, 12553 lines, ~319k tokens (3.04x, diff pasted 3 times): the manifest mentions {{DIFF}} twice. A fix reviewer told 104k tokens to decide whether it fits is handed 319k.
invariant: invariant 8 — a number that does not hold where it is applied
root: substituted text re-substituted as a template

claim: The diff_vol message tells a reviewer who cannot hold the diff to take one half through --scope, but --scope does not shrink the diff it is handed (fix review round 1, R1-003)
scenario: A lead sees the volume line, runs two reviewers with --scope first half / second half; each prompt is 1444765 bytes against 1444645 without --scope (+120), and {{SCOPE_LINE}} tells it to read the rest for context. Only the reporting responsibility halves; the size is unchanged.
invariant: invariant 9 — a document names a way out the mechanism does not provide
root: a document names a way out the mechanism does not provide

claim: Three new negative tests (deferral without reason, reason only in claim, root from the sample) assert the gate's message in check's stdout, never its exit code (fix review round 1, R1-004)
scenario: The deferral gate in cmd_check changed from problems.append to warnings.append: test_отложенная_без_причины_по_прежнему_роняет_проверку stays OK, check exits 0 and a deferral with no reason leaves the review closing with an unsigned risk in it.
invariant: SECURITY.md — check green on a wrong state; class of T3-001
root: a gate whose test asserts its message, not its verdict

claim: The T2 section's opening paragraph follows the last T4 bullet with no blank line in both CHANGELOGs, so it renders as part of the NOTICE.md bullet (fix review round 1, R1-005)
scenario: RELEASING gate 4 takes the release notes from Unreleased verbatim: the reader sees the NOTICE.md entry end with 'Block T2 of the same review — … 15 findings, all closed here.' and the T2 bullets below hang under no heading.

claim: Two of the four places T2-011 fixed — the deferral refusal's tail in check and SKILL.md's completion sentence — are held by no test, and the register records no rule for T2-011 (fix review round 1, R1-006)
scenario: Both reverted to their pre-fix wording, whole suite: 296 tests OK. The refusal again says every deferred finding is fixed or rejected by the end of the review, a claim check does not hold and summary contradicts.
invariant: invariant 2 as applied to the kit itself; lesson 36
root: a document fixed in one place and guarded in another

claim: The verifier's template gets the same whole-block 'read all' file list as the hunter but no {{VOLUME}} reading budget (fix review round 1, R1-007)
scenario: On block T1 the hunter prompt states 'Files: 4. Lines: 4100. ~41k tokens just to read'; the verify prompt has no such line. On a block at the 6000-line ceiling the verifier, the most expensive role (165 → 330 turns), gets no measure and no sentence telling it to say so if it cannot hold the block.
root: the budget stands in one role's assignment and not in another's

claim: vol_over now tells the hunter to name the unread rest in the coverage section, but check reads only the coverage-limits section (fix review round 2, R2-001)
scenario: A block over the 6000-line ceiling: the hunter follows the warning, names the unread files under '## Coverage' and leaves '## Coverage limits' at the skeleton line; check refuses: the coverage-limits section is empty. Same in ru (## Охват vs LIMITS_HEADING). The hunter template still says 'the coverage-limits section below', so the prompt contradicts itself.
invariant: 9 — every gate is announced to the agent by its template
root: a document names a way out the mechanism does not provide

claim: set-finding --rule rewrote the guard of every finding sharing the root: T3-002/012/014 and open T4-021 now name TemplateContractTest, which is green on their defect (fix review round 2, R2-002)
scenario: A bare module-level threshold (FOO_LIMIT = 6 * 7, the shape of T3-014) added to review.py: TemplateContractTest OK, SourceRuleTest FAILED. The register says the class is held by the green test; rule_problem only checks that the file exists, so check is silent.
invariant: 2 — a guard that can be holed with the suite green is not a guard
root: a class recorded as closed by a guard that does not close it

claim: The new glued-paragraph markdown rule refuses correct CommonMark (a heading, table or HTML block after a list item ends the list) and has no invented sample (fix review round 2, R2-003)
scenario: A list item followed directly by '## A heading' renders as a list and a heading, yet the rule flags it as a paragraph glued to the bullet; the rule has no invented-source sample, unlike every other rule in the file.
